What to watch before “Avengers: Doomsday”

Ann Dominique, Contributing Writer
November 10, 2026

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:33
Instaread

As 2026’s cinematic run draws to a close, films such as “Resident Evil” and “The Odyssey” have attracted audiences, while “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” emerged as one of the year’s biggest releases, according to Box Office Mojo. Marvel’s next major film, “Avengers: Doomsday,” brings Robert Downey Jr. back to the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Doctor Doom. Fans speculate that the crossover could mark the end of the MCU’s current era.

“X-Men” (2000) and “X2: X-Men United” (2003)

According to Marvel’s official website, “Avengers: Doomsday” will feature several actors from earlier Marvel films. At the center of the conflict, Fox’s X-Men return for another battle. Watching the original “X-Men” (2000) and “X2: X-Men United” (2003) can help fans refresh their memories of these classic heroes. Patrick Stewart returns as Professor Charles Xavier alongside longtime castmates Ian McKellen (Magneto), Rebecca Romijn (Mystique) and James Marsden (Cyclops).

The X-Men films follow a group of mutant heroes confronting a world that detests them. In “Doomsday,” Doctor Doom could force multiple universes to consider a question the X-Men have faced all along: What are they willing to do to survive? The original cast maintains a large online following despite Marvel’s pursuit of other projects. Fox also faced criticism for giving the franchise rushed, confusing endings. Bringing these characters back could satisfy fans who felt their favorite heroes were left behind.

“Avengers: Infinity War” (2018) and “Avengers: Endgame” (2019)

The release of “Avengers: Infinity War” and “Avengers: Endgame” marked the end of an era for many Marvel fans. In “Infinity War,” the Avengers faced Josh Brolin’s Thanos, who eliminated half of all life in the universe. “Endgame” followed the surviving heroes as they attempted to reverse the destruction and defeat their greatest threat. Iconic characters such as Robert Downey Jr.’s Iron Man and Scarlett Johansson’s Black Widow met their ends, while Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) retired from his role as Captain America.

Marvel subsequently introduced new heroes to the MCU, although longtime Avengers such as Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and the Hulk (Mark Ruffalo) continued appearing in newer projects. With Downey returning as Doctor Doom and Evans reprising his role as Steve Rogers, revisiting both films could help viewers understand the significance of their return.

“Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” (2022)

“Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” established alliances that could face challenges during the battle against Doctor Doom. Revisiting the film can help viewers understand these changing relationships. It introduces Tenoch Huerta Mejía as Namor, ruler of Talokan, and establishes his uneasy alliance with Wakanda. Some fan discussions, including those on Comic Basics, suggest the Wakandans and Talokanil could play major roles in “Doomsday.” Promotional material featuring Namor and Shuri has fueled speculation about their involvement in the MCU’s future.

“Loki” (2021-2023)

At the end of Marvel’s “Loki” series, Tom Hiddleston’s God of Mischief becomes the God of Stories, holding the MCU’s branching timelines together. Hiddleston has confirmed his return in “Doomsday,” creating the possibility of a reunion with Thor. Fans expect an emotional encounter after Hemsworth’s character witnessed his brother’s death in “Avengers: Infinity War” (2018). Loki’s transformation throughout the series gives him an opportunity to demonstrate how much he has changed. Marvel also recommends watching “Loki” before “Doomsday” because it develops his character and explains the conflicts surrounding the multiverse.

“Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” (2022) and “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings” (2021)

“Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness” is another recommended watch because it introduces incursions, catastrophic events involving the collision of two universes. “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings” (2021) also raises unanswered questions about the origins and purpose of the Ten Rings. At the film’s conclusion, the weapons begin emitting a mysterious signal that fans speculate “Doomsday” could explain. Simu Liu will return as Shang-Chi, potentially forming new partnerships with other Avengers.

“Deadpool & Wolverine” (2024)

“Deadpool & Wolverine” (2024) is another useful watch before “Doomsday” because it strengthens the connection between Fox’s X-Men franchise and Marvel’s larger cinematic universe. Deadpool (Ryan Reynolds) and Wolverine (Hugh Jackman) encounter the Time Variance Authority, the same organization that arrested Loki, while learning about variants, the Void and the consequences of disrupting timelines. The film became one of 2024’s highest-grossing releases and demonstrated the audience’s enthusiasm for Marvel’s more mature storytelling. Fans continue hoping to see Reynolds and Jackman reunite in “Doomsday,” although their involvement remains unconfirmed.

“Thunderbolts*” (2025) and “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” (2025)

Two newer MCU additions, “Thunderbolts*” (2025) and “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” (2025), introduce teams expected to play major roles in “Doomsday.” A mid-credits scene in “The Fantastic Four: First Steps” hints at a confrontation involving Doctor Doom and Franklin Richards, the son of Mister Fantastic (Pedro Pascal) and Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby). Franklin possesses extraordinary powers that could make him important to the upcoming conflict.

The Fantastic Four’s ship also appears during the post-credits scene of “Thunderbolts,” entering Earth’s atmosphere. Online theorists have questioned who might be aboard. The Thunderbolts consist of returning characters such as the Winter Soldier, Florence Pugh’s Yelena Belova and David Harbour’s Red Guardian. By the end of the film, the government brands them the New Avengers, creating tension with Sam Wilson’s plans to assemble his own team.

“Captain America: Brave New World” (2025)

Anthony Mackie returns as Captain America in “Doomsday” following “Captain America: Brave New World” (2025). The film follows Sam Wilson as he confronts political conspiracies and global threats while adjusting to his responsibilities as the new Captain America. Its post-credits scene features the Leader (Tim Blake Nelson), who warns of dangers involving other worlds.

Wilson will not be the only Captain America associated with “Doomsday.” Marvel has also confirmed Chris Evans’ return as Steve Rogers. After retiring in “Endgame,” Rogers chose a quiet life with Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell). His return raises questions about how his story could continue and whether he will once again take part in saving the world.

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” (2026)

In “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” (2026), Tom Holland’s Peter Parker fights crime in a world that no longer remembers him. Although Holland’s involvement in “Doomsday” remains unconfirmed, fans speculate that Spider-Man’s story could connect to “Avengers: Secret Wars” (2027). The franchise has already explored alternate versions of Peter Parker through Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield’s appearances in “Spider-Man: No Way Home” (2021). Their return demonstrated that different versions of familiar heroes could share the screen, leaving audiences hopeful for another crossover.

What does “Doomsday” mean for the MCU?

Marvel has hinted that these storylines will connect in “Doomsday.” Teams such as the Thunderbolts, the Fantastic Four and the X-Men may find themselves working alongside the Avengers. Their combined knowledge and abilities could prove essential to defeating Doctor Doom, provided they can put aside their differences.

Fan speculation on platforms such as X and TikTok suggests a bleak future for some of the original Avengers. Many expect their favorite characters’ stories to conclude when the film premieres in December. Still, completing those character arcs could satisfy longtime fans while making room for a new generation of heroes. Younger characters could help new audiences connect with the MCU and give Marvel opportunities to develop different stories.

Regardless of how “Doomsday” ends, audiences will likely anticipate the Avengers’ return in “Avengers: Secret Wars,” the sixth installment in the franchise. With “Doomsday” scheduled to open Dec. 18, Marvel’s recommended viewing list gives fans an opportunity to revisit the stories that could shape the MCU’s next major chapter.
